cuts.name: primary
cuts.note: The only analysis with a protected significance level. One-sided p = 0.0266 against a prespecified one-sided alpha of 0.10. The same result two-sided is p = 0.053, so it met the bar the trial set and would not have met a conventional two-sided 0.05.
cuts.source: AACR 2023 abstract CT001; Weber et al., Lancet 2024;403(10427):632-644.

cuts.name: year3
cuts.note: Nominal. No alpha was assigned to this analysis. No Kaplan-Meier figure with an at-risk table was published for this cutoff, so it is quoted, never reconstructed.
cuts.source: ASCO 2024 abstract LBA9512; Carlino et al., JCO Oncol Adv 2026;3(1):e2500008.

cuts.name: year5
cuts.note: Nominal. The analysis this project reconstructs, because it publishes a censoring column that makes the reconstruction exact at interval level.
cuts.source: ASCO 2026 abstract 9500; Khattak et al., J Clin Oncol 2026;44(26):2482-2489.

caveats: It says nothing about absolute risk. A halving of a small risk is a small change in how many people are affected.
It is an average over time. If the benefit grows or shrinks, one number hides that.
hazard_ratio.plain: A hazard ratio compares how quickly something is happening in two groups. A hazard ratio of 0.51 means that at any given moment, people who got the vaccine plus the antibody were recurring at about half the rate of people who got the antibody alone. It is a comparison of speeds, not a promise about any individual, and not a statement that half as many people recurred overall.
sources: Cox DR, J R Stat Soc B 1972;34(2):187-220.
hazard_ratio.technical: The ratio of instantaneous event rates between arms, estimated here by a Cox proportional hazards model. It is an average over the whole follow-up period and assumes the ratio is roughly constant throughout.
hazard_ratio.title: What a hazard ratio is

caveats: They are the same patients each time, not three independent findings.
nominal_p_values.plain: The trial has been analysed three times as follow-up lengthened: the p-value went 0.0266, then 0.019, then 0.0075. It is tempting to read that as the evidence getting stronger. It is not that. Only the first analysis had a pre-agreed threshold. The later ones are extra looks at the same 157 patients, with no correction for having looked repeatedly, and the presentation itself says no significance level was assigned to them.
nominal_p_values.technical: The three-year and five-year analyses are nominal and descriptive, with no alpha allocated and no multiplicity adjustment. Repeated analyses of accumulating data inflate the chance of a small p-value even when nothing is happening.
nominal_p_values.title: Why the later p-values are not what they look like

caveats: NNT depends entirely on the timepoint chosen. Quoting one without a timepoint is meaningless.
number_needed_to_treat.plain: Number needed to treat answers: how many people would have to get this treatment for one extra person to benefit? Here it is about 5 at five years. But the honest version includes the uncertainty, and that runs from about 3 to about 78. 'Somewhere between 3 and 78' is the real state of knowledge, and it is a much weaker claim than '5'.
number_needed_to_treat.technical: The reciprocal of the absolute risk difference. When the risk difference's confidence interval includes zero, the reciprocal is not an interval at all but two rays extending to infinity, and must be reported as a number needed to benefit together with a number needed to harm. This project's result type cannot express a finite upper bound in that case.
number_needed_to_treat.title: Number needed to treat, and why its interval looks strange

caveats: A one-sided test only looks for benefit. It cannot, by construction, find harm.

Phase 2 trials often use looser thresholds deliberately, to decide whether a Phase 3 is worth running. That is a reasonable design choice, but it means the result is a reason to keep going, not a conclusion.
one_sided_alpha.plain: Before it started, the trial decided what would count as a positive result: a one-sided p-value below 0.10. That is a more forgiving threshold than the two-sided 0.05 most people have in mind. The headline p-value of 0.0266 cleared the bar the trial set. The same result stated the conventional way is p = 0.053, which would not have cleared the usual one. Both of those are true, and this project states both every time.
one_sided_alpha.technical: Designed for 80% power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.5 at an overall one-sided alpha of 0.10, requiring at least 40 recurrence events. The primary analysis occurred at 44 events.
one_sided_alpha.title: The bar this trial set itself

caveats: Distant metastasis-free survival is somewhat more robust, being harder to miss or dispute, and it moved in the same direction.
The size of any such bias is unknown and cannot be estimated from the published data.
open_label.plain: Everyone in this trial knew which treatment they were getting, and so did their doctors. That matters more than it sounds, because the thing being measured is 'has the cancer come back?' -- which depends on when somebody orders a scan and how they read it. Expectation can shift both. The Phase 3 trial fixed this by giving everyone an injection, with half of them a placebo.
open_label.technical: Open-label design with investigator-assessed recurrence-free survival as the primary endpoint, creating potential for ascertainment and assessment bias in the direction of the expected effect.
open_label.title: Nobody was blinded

caveats: Nothing in this repository uses any Phase 3 efficacy figure, because none has been published.
The product is not approved by any regulator anywhere.
phase_3.plain: A much larger Phase 3 trial of about 1,100 patients has already reported that it met its goals, in August 2026. That is the trial that actually settles this question: it is bigger, and everyone in it received an injection so nobody knew who got the vaccine. But no actual numbers from it have been published yet. 'It met its endpoints' is not a number, and this project does not pretend otherwise.
phase_3.technical: INTerpath-001 (NCT05933577): 1,137 patients randomised 2:1, double-blind against placebo plus pembrolizumab, met recurrence-free and distant metastasis-free survival at a pre-specified interim analysis. No hazard ratio, confidence interval or p-value is in the public domain as of 2026-10-18.
phase_3.title: The real test is already finished, and not yet public

caveats: Failing to detect a violation is not the same as showing there is none. With 51 events this test would miss most realistic departures.
proportional_hazards.plain: Summarising a whole trial with one hazard ratio assumes the gap between the two groups stays in roughly the same proportion over time. If the vaccine's benefit only appears after two years, or fades after four, a single number hides that shape.
proportional_hazards.technical: Tested with Schoenfeld residuals. On this reconstruction the test does not detect a violation, but with about fifty events it has very little power to do so. Restricted mean survival time is reported alongside the hazard ratio because it requires no such assumption.
proportional_hazards.title: The assumption behind the hazard ratio

caveats: No subgroup, covariate or dose-response claim can be supported by reconstructed data.
reconstruction_limits.plain: The patient-level data in this project was rebuilt from published summary tables. It reproduces the trial's published results closely, but nobody in it is a real person. It can be used to re-examine the headline numbers. It cannot be used to ask new questions, like whether the vaccine worked better in one subgroup.
sources: Guyot P et al., BMC Med Res Methodol 2012;12:9.
reconstruction_limits.technical: Reconstructed from the published at-risk and cumulative-censoring columns, which determine the event counts in each interval exactly. The remaining freedom is where events fall within an interval, and the reported sensitivity analysis shows the hazard ratio moves by under 0.01 across reasonable choices. The published hazard ratio comes from a model stratified by disease stage; the reconstruction has no stage variable and is therefore unstratified, which is an irreducible source of difference.
reconstruction_limits.title: What reconstructed data can and cannot tell you

caveats: This project refuses to reconstruct the survival curve for exactly this reason: a curve drawn through 14 events would look like a finding.
rfs_is_not_survival.plain: What this trial measured is how long people went without the cancer coming back. That is worth having on its own. But it is not the same as living longer, and this trial cannot tell us about that: there were 7 deaths in each group, 14 in total. You cannot learn much from 14 events. Anyone citing the survival numbers from this trial is overreaching.
rfs_is_not_survival.technical: Recurrence-free survival is the primary endpoint. Overall survival is exploratory, with a hazard ratio of 0.471 and a 95% interval from 0.165 to 1.345 -- an interval that includes both substantial benefit and modest harm. Recurrence-free survival has not been validated as a trial-level surrogate for overall survival in adjuvant melanoma.
rfs_is_not_survival.title: Staying cancer-free is not the same as living longer

caveats: Small positive trials systematically overstate effects, because a small trial only reaches significance when the observed effect is large.
small_sample.plain: The trial randomised 157 people, and after five years 51 of them had had a recurrence. Everything here rests on those 51 events. That is why the confidence interval is so wide: the data are compatible with the vaccine roughly tripling the time people stay cancer-free, and also with a much more modest benefit.
small_sample.technical: Hazard ratio 0.51 with a 95% confidence interval of 0.294 to 0.887. The interval excludes 1, but spans a wide range of effect sizes. Number needed to treat at five years is about 5, with an interval running past 70.
small_sample.title: 157 patients, 51 events

proportional_hazards.caveat: Tested on 51 events, which gives this check very little power. A non-significant result means no violation was detected, not that the assumption holds.

checks.note: published as not estimable; a finite value would contradict it

verdict: This is a genuinely promising result and it is not proof. A 157-patient, open-label Phase 2b trial found that adding a personalized vaccine to pembrolizumab left about 20 more people per 100 cancer-free at five years. The trial met the bar it set itself, which was a one-sided p below 0.10 -- a more forgiving threshold than the conventional one, which the same result would not have cleared. Nobody was blinded, the later analyses were not statistically protected, and with 14 deaths in total the trial says nothing about living longer. The biology is plausible and the direction is consistent across endpoints. The larger, blinded Phase 3 trial has reported that it met its goals, but has published no numbers. That trial, not this one, is the test.
